leads.name: National champion swamp tupelo
leads.note: American Forests reports it as national champion (337 points), 5-foot-thick trunk, 80 ft to first limb, 'growing on the bank of a small muddy creek deep in the heart of Congaree'. No trail, no coordinate, no public path found this pass. Needs a precise location before it could be a collectible point.

leads.name: National champion sweetgum
leads.note: 203in circumference, 160ft tall, near Cedar Creek in 'trackless, eastern wilderness', described as hidden by understory. No public trail access and no coordinate found; blocked-leaning rather than a lead, but keeping as a lead in case a trail or coordinate turns up.

leads.name: Former national champion laurel oak
leads.note: Reached only 'after a three-mile hike' per American Forests; no trail name or coordinate found this pass.

leads.name: State champion bald cypress, east end of park
leads.note: Friends of Congaree Swamp essay 'Congaree's Cypress Story': nearly 28ft circumference, 132ft tall, 'east end' of the park, reached via Bates Ferry Trail. May be the same tree as the Harry Hampton Tree (cgr_002, delivered) given similar figures, or a distinct second champion cypress; not resolved this pass. Worth a follow-up pass to disambiguate before treating as a separate entry.

leads.name: Tallest loblolly pine on Weston Lake Loop near Bridge D
leads.note: Oakridge Trail Guide (Friends of Congaree) separately mentions 'a large loblolly pine on the Weston Lake Loop Trail near Bridge D... almost 170 feet tall, tallest tree in South Carolina', which may be the true current national-champion loblolly (172ft/15ft circumference per the Cely essay) rather than the Richland County Pine (cgr_001, over 150ft, a FORMER state champion per NPS stop 11). These read as two distinct loblollies. Needs a follow-up pass to pin an exact coordinate near Bridge D and confirm it is not the same tree as cgr_001 before delivering.
